paragraphs.text: Good morning, sisters and elders. What a wonderful day to be a missionary.
As I've been reading your letters this week, I'm just being so inspired by you and your devotion to the Lord and your faith in His power to empower us and protect us. You are remarkable.
Thanks for praying for Sister Hughes and me, and please know that we are praying for you.

Today, I've received many emails from the missionaries who have returned home. They're in a 14-day quarantine, and they're missing you and the work here in the Philippines so very much. Many of them are praying that a cure will be found quickly so that they can return to their areas here and get back to work. I believe those prayers will be answered.
I'm just feeling more and more optimistic. As I've read these heartfelt emails, I was prompted to ask these wonderful missionaries to do just what I asked you to do.

I asked them to video record their best three- to five-minute version of Lessons 1 through 5 in Tagalog, then to send those videos to me. I think we'll be seeing a lot of these videos come in, and you'll be able to give them feedback so that they can stay sharp in their language skills and their teaching skills.

I think some of the more experienced missionaries will be sharing some of their best tips in these videos as well. Why not have them learning the same things we are learning? Maybe some of them will be back with us in a month or two so that they can finish their missions in the best mission in the world.
Today I'm going to be trying to get up to San Jose del Monte. We have so many empty apartments with food and water in them, and I want that food and water for you in case we need it.
The key principle in times like these is to hope for the best while preparing for the worst.

Again, I remind you to make sure that I know if you don't have three jugs of water for every missionary in your apartment and also 14 days of food for each missionary in your apartment. Also, don't let your water get too low before you reorder. I would suggest that you reorder when you are down to two full jugs left. That way you will always have plenty of water on hand.
Now, how are your videos going? Are you getting better? I would love each companionship to send me one of their best videos. I want to enjoy your progress.

The Area Presidency is getting reports that members are loving your work, and they contacted me to ask if it was okay with me that they share what we are doing with all the other mission presidents. Of course, I said no problem. We're happy to share anything that will be helpful.
As I wrap up this short update, I just want to remind you to be very wise in your activities when you go out of the apartment. Be sure to go straight to the store and back.

The government authorities are very serious, and if they think you are not following the rules, they have the power to detain you, and it may be very difficult to resolve the situation and get you out of that detention.

So be wise. Also maintain social distancing. That means two meters' distance from other people, and always wear your mask. We have more masks, so don't be shy to ask for another one if yours is getting old.

Sisters and elders, we love you. We look forward to getting back to normal, and I believe that could be not too far away for us. Just my opinion, but for now, let's make the most of our time to serve and grow stronger, better, and smarter as online ministers.
We want to minister in every way we can so that we'll be prepared to go stronger when the times change.
Now one more idea: be happy.
Happiness is a choice. It will always be a choice, and you get to choose whether you're going to be a happy person or not a happy person. And it's a lot more fun to be happy.
Choose to be happy. Choose to be healthy. Choose to be strong. And you'll be so very grateful that you became an agent of change for yourself and not something to be acted upon.
I love you all. I'm proud of you. Let's make this a great day.
